transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-17 11:00 PT / 14:00 ET
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (Palisade CTO), Priya Desai (Lead ML Eng), Ravi Menon (PM)

[00:00] Jordan Park: Alright, hey everyone thanks for joining. quick agenda, we'll run through the scorecard, call out any regressions, talk guardrails and next steps. Maya and I are here from Redwood. Tom, Priya, Ravi, you good?

[00:12] Tom Alvarez: Yeah, good, thanks. we got a bit of context — saw the notes from last week, so hoping we can narrow down the spike in "incorrect matches" we've been seeing.

[00:22] Priya Desai: Hey, yeah real quick — we threw in that new product-matching prompt variant last monday and the false positive rate jumped, so we want to figure out if it's prompt logic or model drift.

[00:34] Maya Singh: Totally, and that's what we want to hunt today. we pulled the week-over-week metrics, and there's a clear uptick starting 48 hours after the prompt push.

[00:45] Jordan Park: I'll share my screen with the scorecard — bear with me while I pull it up. (screen share) okay, main things: precision down from 0.91 to 0.77 on product match intent, hallucination index up from 0.03 to 0.12 on the same set.

[01:05] Ravi Menon: Wow, that's bigger than we expected. Are those for the hosted lane or dedicated?

[01:11] Maya Singh: These are for hosted default run. we didn't schedule a dedicated run after the prompt change, so first pass is from hosted. but the payloads and truncate lengths are identical.

[01:22] Priya Desai: Could it be related to the new temperature setting we tried? we nudged it from 0.0 to 0.2 for variety.

[01:30] Maya Singh: Good flag — we have an annotation in the sheet that a temp bump was in the canary. Still, the pattern looks prompt-shift heavy; the examples failing are near-exact matches that the previous prompt handled fine.

[01:45] Tom Alvarez: Do we have raw examples? like a sample of false positives?

[01:48] Jordan Park: Yes Priya has them — Priya, did you paste the 30 sample cases in the doc?

[01:52] Priya Desai: I pasted a set of 40, but we're prepping 200 exports — I'll upload after the call. some transcription note: a couple of the examples include SKU codes with dashes, and sometimes the model seems to conflate that with category names.

[02:10] Maya Singh: Okay, that helps. two-pronged approach recommended: 1) targeted bisection of prompt variants (roll back to previous prompt, then incremental changes), 2) run a quantized 4-bit variant to ensure behavior is consistent across model artifacts. we've seen cases where a quant+kernel path can surface different tokenization edge cases.

[02:35] Tom Alvarez: Wait — quantization changed behavior historically? we thought quant was just perf/cost tradeoff.

[02:40] Maya Singh: Usually yes but subtle differences in floating point can slightly change logits ordering in close-call cases. not common but for high-precision product matching it can matter.

[02:50] Ravi Menon: Interesting. ok so what's the action then?

[02:55] Jordan Park: We'll run bisection on three prompts: current canary, previous stable, and a hybrid with the SKU-normalization step. Maya will also spin up a 4-bit quant run on the same sample set and compare.

[03:10] Priya Desai: For the SKU-normalization, we're basically running a pre-step that strips punctuation and runs a lookup table, right?

[03:16] Maya Singh: Yes, exactly. simple normalization usually helps. but we also want to check guardrail hitting — if guardrail kicked in differently after prompt change, that could explain the mismatch.

[03:30] Tom Alvarez: Can you remind me what guardrails are live? We have the high-confidence suppression and the domain whitelist, right?

[03:36] Jordan Park: Right now: 1) domain whitelist for product categories, 2) confidence threshold at 0.65, 3) an explicit blocklist for some brand names. we also have a prefix-based prefix cache — oh sorry, prefix caching — that may affect short-query hot paths. sometimes transcription shows it as K-V cash or K-V cache in our logs, so names get munged in the exported tables.

[04:02] Priya Desai: Yeah we've seen inconsistent hits on the domain whitelist when the model rewrites queries.

[04:08] Maya Singh: That is another vector — model rewrite can cause the predicted token stream to no longer align with whitelist regex. we'll instrument a log to capture pre/post rewrite tokens.

[04:18] Ravi Menon: Question on security — if we run the dedicated pilot or move examples to Redwood for debugging, what's the retention and KMS stance? we have strict rules.

[04:26] Jordan Park: Good point. Redwood's hosted POC tier keeps data for 30 days by default; we can enable a shorter retention, and we support customer-managed keys (KMS). For Private/Dedicated you can control retention fully and use HSM-backed KMS. we'll send the SOC2 section of the security brief.

[04:42] Tom Alvarez: Send that please. Also we need to know whether your audit logs capture token-level traces or just request/response hashes.

[04:49] Maya Singh: We capture per-request metadata, timestamps, and optionally token-level outputs if you opt in — we can redact PII automatically. will include specifics in the security doc.

[04:58] Priya Desai: Back to regression: do you think the prompt change could have introduced a degenerate rewrite that increases hallucination?

[05:06] Maya Singh: Yes that's consistent. Example we flagged where the model inserted an extra predicate like "best selling" which mapped to a different product cluster. It looks like a subtle prompt phrasing change nudged the model's completion anchor.

[05:18] Jordan Park: To be concrete: plan is run a bisection on the 200 failing examples. we'll run each prompt variant with identical runtime configs: same max tokens, same temp, same truncation, and capture top-5 logits where available. Maya will also run the 4-bit quant job to compare.

[05:36] Tom Alvarez: Sounds good. What about scoring — are we using precision@1 only or NDCG?

[05:42] Maya Singh: For product-match we typically report precision@1 and a weighted NDCG for ranked lists. we'll include both in the sheet. the current pivot shows precision@1 drop as the most alarming.

[05:54] Ravi Menon: If the regression is truly prompt-driven, what's the rollback story in hosted? can we pin the old prompt quickly?

[06:00] Jordan Park: Yes, in hosted we can pin the route configuration to the stable prompt and roll out a canary with the change pending validation. it's a config flip. For dedicated it's typically a release window but we can patch canary config too.

[06:12] Priya Desai: Ok please do not flip anything until we see the bisection results. we need the failing set to be the source of truth.

[06:18] Jordan Park: Absolutely. we'll hold changes.

[06:22] Maya Singh: One more nuance — we saw a small subset of examples where the model returned an exact SKU but the downstream rules rated it as low confidence due to mismatched casing or punctuation; normalization will likely fix that in a rule-based way without touching model.

[06:38] Tom Alvarez: Good, if we can fix 30% of cases with normalization that's win. For the rest we'll need model fixes.

[06:44] Jordan Park: Timeline: Maya runs bisection and quant compare (ETA 48-72 hours), Priya to upload 200 fails (ETA tomorrow), Jordan shares updated sheet and guardrail links (by EOD tomorrow). We reconvene next Wednesday at same time for the verdict.

[06:58] Ravi Menon: Quick procurement note — we're approaching the budget sign-off; if Dedicated shows predictable improvements we can move faster. Also curious about per-token economics on the quantized run.

[07:06] Maya Singh: We'll add an economics tab: cost per query for hosted baseline vs 4-bit quant vs dedicated reserved throughput. should help the business case.

[07:14] Tom Alvarez: Cool. any blockers from Redwood's side?

[07:18] Jordan Park: No blockers. we'll need the failing set and any priority intents labeled. Also, if you want, we can run a small A/B on the canary traffic for live comparisons once we have regression mitigations staged.

[07:30] Priya Desai: Let's keep live A/B to the end — first bisection then internal evaluation.

[07:35] Jordan Park: Sounds good. last callouts: we'll include the security brief, the audit log spec, and the guardrail rule examples in GH link in the sheet. Oh and apologies for any mis-transcribed terms in the sheet earlier — sometimes our export munges VPC into NPC in the export, so watch for that.

[07:50] Tom Alvarez: Haha okay noted.

[07:52] Jordan Park: Alright folks, thanks everyone. recap in the sheet and action items assigned. see you next week.

[07:58] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-generated with occasional mislabels and missing punctuation. Some proper nouns (e.g., SKU formatting, prefix cache) may be imperfect.
